answer: An island cannot fake its own census. Each identity must climb a knoll: a memory-hard sequential proof, un-splittable across machines, so N clones cost N full climbs with no batching discount. Every climb is witnessed by a fable, a chain of honest acts, each chapter signed by an elder of a different island and hashed to the climber's address. The bond grows with how many identities share one island: the k-th member posts k units, so N clones packed together pay about N squared, while spreading out forces the attacker to bribe many independent elders. A cheat burns the whole island bond.
